brief: Three stress points combined to drive a broad risk-off move. France led, with the Franco-German 10yr spread widening to 174bps (near its November 2011, 189bps single-currency-era peak) as ECB hike odds for December fell to 69% from 90%. Italian spreads and European HY spreads (369bps, widest since April 2025) widened in sympathy, while STOXX Banks hit a 4-month low. Second, fresh AI growth fears hit the Philly semiconductor index, CoreWeave (equity and CDS) and Meta, whose post-earnings rally reversed as capex sentiment soured, dragging the S&P 500 and Nasdaq to their worst sessions since July and June even as defensive sectors and the equal-weighted index outperformed. Third, Middle East escalation risk (a reported US-Israel strike plan against Iran, a Houthi attack claim) pushed Brent to a 5-month high. Treasuries rallied despite strong jobless-claims data, showing stress outweighing fundamentals. Overnight, the selloff has stabilised: US and European futures and most Asian indices are only slightly lower, while Japan's core CPI rose above target.
